summary: T-0658 [security/системный, столп 4]: fail-closed `AND deactivated_at IS NULL` on EVERY live subject->authority resolver, so a deactivated (fired) employee whose already-issued KC access token is still within its TTL (KC enabled:false blocks only NEW token issuance, not an already-issued one before expiry — a window of minutes) loses ALL authorization inside Choros. ROUND 1 closed the GRANT path (getGrantsForSubject step 1, grants-dao.ts): the single canonical resolver every ordinary PDP consumer uses (invoke.ts, records.ts field/read-visibility, org.ts capability-token, sandbox-gate-dao.ts, capability-grants-dao.ts, registry-digest-dao.ts). ROUND 2 (CHANGES_REQUESTED — adversarial skeptic REAL_HOLE, severity HIGH): the round-1 ripple analysis relied on `grep getGrantsForSubject` and FALSELY claimed 'closes the gap for every consumer'. Owner/admin authority is resolved by a SECOND, PARALLEL resolver in src/db/org.ts (isGenesisOwnerForTenant / loadAdminContext) that grep never found, and owner authority SHORT-CIRCUITS the grant PDP (capability-grants-dao.ts: `if (await isGenesisOwnerForTenant(...)) return true;` runs BEFORE getGrantsForSubject). Deactivation only sets employee.deactivated_at — it does NOT revoke the tenant-owner role_assignment — so a deactivated OWNER (the most-privileged subject, exactly the 'fired, token still live' threat) with a live token kept full owner authority: seed-write employee/org mutation (x11), LLM-key config, system-agent operation, mgmt_object delegation, SoD-admin. Round 2 adds the same fail-closed predicate to the THREE inline slug->employee subqueries in org.ts (isGenesisOwnerForTenant + loadAdminContext owner-check + loadAdminContext assignment-load), which closes the ENTIRE owner/admin surface at the source (all ~11 seed-write mgmt paths + llm-config.ts + report-page-render.ts + rights-sod-admin.ts + pdp-explain.ts funnel through these two functions — verified by grep). It also closes a THIRD parallel resolver: report-page-render.ts::defaultCheckReadGrant non-owner branch had its own inline slug->employee + application:read grant read (not via getGrantsForSubject) — a deactivated delegated-reader could still render report pages. Human vs agent unchanged from round 1: deactivated_at is structurally never set for kind='agent' (only writer PATCH /api/users is human-only), so every gate is a permanent no-op for legitimate agents and a real fail-closed gate for humans. Ripple analysis (ADR §3.1-3.4) now enumerates ALL THREE resolvers + explicitly triages every other inline slug->employee subquery as non-authority (SoD restriction-readers, display lists, identity-mapping, write-target existence) — none needing (some actively harmed by) the gate.

findings_out_of_scope: pdp-explain.ts (src/http/pdp-explain.ts:119) — the DIAGNOSTIC explain endpoint loads the subject's grants via its own local grant-source WITHOUT the deactivation gate. This is NOT a security hole: the endpoint's OWN authz is loadAdminContext (now gated round 2) + self-query, so a deactivated actor cannot explain another subject. But a self-query explain by a deactivated actor could DISPLAY grants the real PDP (grant path) no longer honors — an explain-FIDELITY divergence (diagnostics lying), not an authorization grant. Aligning explain fidelity with the real PDP is a separate follow-up (ADR §9). Not fixed here because it authorizes nothing.

inbox.ts local deactivation gates (T-0588 BLOCK-3 claim ~1413-1417, RE-VERIFY approve ~1631-1643) are now redundant defence-in-depth rather than the sole line of defence (the grant resolver is fail-closed). Left in place per additive-only instruction; removal is a separate simplification follow-up.

This fix closes the PDP-resolution/short-circuit gap inside Choros only. It does NOT shorten or revoke the underlying live KC access token — the window between deactivation and that token's TTL expiry still exists at the AUTHENTICATION layer (a deactivated user can still present a valid token and authenticate; every AUTHORIZATION decision now correctly denies them in that window). KC session/token revocation on deactivation is a separate, larger task (spec §7).

src/db/sod-dao.ts:395 and src/http/rights-sod.ts:273 deliberately NOT gated — SoD is a RESTRICTION (separation of duties), not a grant; adding the gate would drop a deactivated subject's assignments and thus SUPPRESS a SoD violation (fail-OPEN for the restriction). Their grant authority is already [] via the round-1 grant-path gate. Documented in ADR §3.4.
